question: A ball of mass 0.50 kg moves horizontally rightwards at 20.0 m·s⁻¹ and strikes a vertical concrete wall. It rebounds horizontally to the left at a speed of 15.0 m·s⁻¹. question: An arrow of height h_o = 8.0 cm is placed upright at a distance of d_o = 40.0 cm from a thin CONVEX lens having a focal length of f = +20.0 cm. Calculate the HEIGHT (h_i) of the resulting image:

explanation: 1. Image distance: 1/d_i = 1/f - 1/d_o = 1/20.0 - 1/40.0 => d_i = (800.0) / (20.0) = 40.00 cm. 2. Magnification: |m| = d_i / d_o = 40.00 / 40.0 = 1.000. 3. Image height: h_i = |m| × h_o = 1.000 × 8.0 cm = 8.00 cm (Inverted real image).

tags.subject: Technical Sciences
tags.learning_outcome: Calculate image height from multi-step lens equation

question: A power supply of EMF ε = 6.0 V and internal resistance r = 0.40 Ω is connected to a circuit drawing a current of 0.71 A. Calculate the operating TERMINAL VOLTAGE (V_terminal) available to the external circuit:
wrong_answers_pool: 6.0 V (neglected internal resistance: assumed zero lost volts)
0.29 V (calculated lost volts instead of terminal voltage)

question: A stationary equipment trolley of mass 10 kg is pulled across a rough horizontal concrete floor by an applied horizontal force of 800 N through a displacement of 30.0 m. The coefficient of kinetic friction is μ_k = 0.20. Using the Work-Energy Theorem (W_net = ΔE_k), calculate the final velocity of the trolley (g = 9.8 m·s⁻²):
wrong_answers_pool: 4682.40 m·s⁻¹ (forgot to take square root of vf²)
48.39 m·s⁻¹ (omitted factor of 2 in kinetic energy)
